metadata.title: A $ \sup + C \inf $ inequality on a domain of $ {\mathbb R}^2 $.

extraction_notes.note: Equations are hand-numbered with '\qquad (E)', '(1)', '(***)' inside $$...$$ (no \eqno), so latex_facts did not report them; emitted as equation nodes since the text cites them.
definition or problem: the PDE setting (E),(*),(**) is referred to as 'the previous problem' but is a hypothesis setup, not a computational problem.
Author's '{\bf Remark}' is content-wise an example of case 1) of the theorem; typed example.
Theorem 1.2 is called 'theorem 1' and 'theorem 2' in the text; Example 1.1 is 'Example 1'; resolved by content.
The prose argument for Corollary 2.2 ends with 'that,' running into the corollary environment.
Radial-case argument states and proves its conclusion in one go with no separately stated claim; kept as one remark.

metadata.extraction_comment: The second half of the paper is a list of questions answered by counterexamples; questions are open_problem nodes and the counterexamples example nodes linked by illustrates.

nodes.name: Laplacian and domain Omega
nodes.statement: We set $ \Delta = \partial_{11} + \partial_{22} $ on open set $ \Omega $ of $ {\mathbb R}^2 $ with a smooth boundary.
nodes.statement_short: Laplacian $\Delta=\partial_{11}+\partial_{22}$ on a smooth bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$.

nodes.name: Prescribed scalar curvature problem (E) with conditions (*), (**)
nodes.statement: Let's consider a sequence of functions solutions to: $$ -\Delta u_i=V_i(x) e^{u_i}\,\, \qquad (E) $$ with, $$ 0 \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \qquad (*)$$ $$ \int_{\Omega} e^{u_i} dx \leq C, \qquad (**)$$
nodes.statement_short: Sequences $u_i$ solving $-\Delta u_i=V_ie^{u_i}$ with $0\le V_i\le b$ and $\int e^{u_i}\le C$ ('the previous problem').

nodes.name: Equation (E)
nodes.statement: $$ -\Delta u_i=V_i(x) e^{u_i}\,\, \qquad (E) $$

nodes.name: Condition (*)
nodes.statement: $$ 0 \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \qquad (*)$$

nodes.name: Condition (**)
nodes.statement: $$ \int_{\Omega} e^{u_i} dx \leq C, \qquad (**)$$

nodes.name: Brezis-Merle alternative (Theorem A)
nodes.statement: {\bf Theorem A}. {\it We have the following alternative: 1) $ (u_i)_i $ is uniformly locally bounded, \smallskip or, \smallskip 2) $ u_i \to - \infty $ on each compact set of $ \Omega $, \smallskip or, \smallskip 3) There is a finite set (of blow-up points) $ S=\{ x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_m \} \subset \Omega $ and sequences of points $ (x_k^i)_i $ such that, $$ x_k^i \to x_k, \,\,\, u_i(x_k^i) \to + \infty $$ and, in the sense of distributions we have: $$ V_i e^{u_i} \to \sum_{k=0}^m \alpha_k \delta_{x_k}, \,\,\alpha_k \geq 4\pi, $$ and, $$ u_i \to - \infty , \,\, { \rm on \, each \, compact \, set \, of }\,\, \Omega-S. $$ }
conclusions: 2) $ u_i \to - \infty $ on each compact set of $ \Omega $

3) There is a finite set (of blow-up points) $ S=\{ x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_m \} \subset \Omega $ and sequences of points $ (x_k^i)_i $ such that, $$ x_k^i \to x_k, \,\,\, u_i(x_k^i) \to + \infty $$ and, in the sense of distributions we have: $$ V_i e^{u_i} \to \sum_{k=0}^m \alpha_k \delta_{x_k}, \,\,\alpha_k \geq 4\pi, $$ and, $$ u_i \to - \infty , \,\, { \rm on \, each \, compact \, set \, of }\,\, \Omega-S. $$
nodes.statement_short: Solutions of (E) under (*),(**) are locally bounded, tend to $-\infty$ locally uniformly, or blow up at finitely many points with mass $\ge4\pi$.

nodes.name: Existence of a sup + C inf inequality
nodes.statement: Here, we are interested by to know if, we can have an inequality of type: $$ \sup_{\Omega} u_i + C_1 \inf_K u_i \geq - C_2, $$ where $ C_1 $ and $ C_2 $ are two positive constant which depend only on $ b, C, K $ and $ \Omega $.
nodes.statement_short: Is $\sup_\Omega u_i + C_1\inf_K u_i \ge -C_2$ with constants depending only on $b,C,K,\Omega$?

nodes.name: Nash-Moser scheme does not apply; Green function lower bound
nodes.statement: We have the following result which express that we can not apply the Nash-Moser iterate scheme to prove the existence of a lower bound for $ \sup + \inf $ inequality. We need other arguments to obtain such estimate. Note that, in dimension $ n \geq 3 $, and, in the case of a compact riemannian manifold, we need the existence of a lower bound of the Green function to have a $ \sup \times \inf $ inequality.
nodes.statement_short: The example shows Nash-Moser iteration cannot give sup+inf bounds; in dimension $\ge3$ a Green function lower bound gives sup x inf.

nodes.name: sup + C inf inequality on a domain of R^2
nodes.statement: Let $ (u_i) $ and $ (V_i) $ two sequences of functions solutions to the previous problem, then \bigskip 1) For all compact $ K $ of $ \Omega $ we have: $$ \sup_K u_i \to -\infty $$ or, \smallskip 2) For all compact $ K \subset \Omega $, there are two positive constants $ C_1= C_1(dist(K, \partial \Omega), b, C) $ and $ C_2=C_2(K, \Omega, b, C) $ such that: $$ \sup_{\Omega } u_i + C_1\inf_K u_i \geq -C_2 $$
assumptions: $ (u_i) $ and $ (V_i) $ two sequences of functions solutions to the previous problem
conclusions: 1) For all compact $ K $ of $ \Omega $ we have: $$ \sup_K u_i \to -\infty $$

2) For all compact $ K \subset \Omega $, there are two positive constants $ C_1= C_1(dist(K, \partial \Omega), b, C) $ and $ C_2=C_2(K, \Omega, b, C) $ such that: $$ \sup_{\Omega } u_i + C_1\inf_K u_i \geq -C_2 $$
nodes.statement_short: Either $\sup_K u_i\to-\infty$ on every compact $K$, or $\sup_\Omega u_i + C_1\inf_K u_i\ge -C_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Example 1
nodes.statement:
\underbar {Proof of the Example 1: Nullity of the lower bound of the Green function.}  igskip We want to prove by contradiction that:  igskip For all $ 1 > \epsilon >0 $ and $ \gamma >0 $ , there is a constant $ c= c(b, C, \epsilon, \gamma) $ such that: $$ \gamma u_i(0) + u_i(\epsilon) 	o + \infty, $$ For this, we consider the function: $$ v_i=e^{u_i} $$ $$ -\Delta v_i + |
abla u_i|^2 v_i= v_i^2. $$ Also, we can write: $$ -\Delta v_i + (1+ |
abla u_i|^2) v_i= v_i^2+ v_i, $$ And, $$ \inf_{B_k(0)} v_i \geq \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} G_i(y_i,y)(v_i^2+ v_i ) dy $$ Thus, by contradiction, we suppose that: $$ \lim_i \left ( \inf_{x, y \in B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} G_i(x,y)ight ) > c >0, $$ thus, $$ \sup_{B_1(0)} e^{\gamma u_i} 	imes v_i (k) \geq c \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)}(v_i^{2+\gamma}+ v_i^{1+\gamma} ) dy, $$ If we argue by contradiction, and suppose that $ \sup + \inf $ is finite: $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} v_i^{1+\gamma} dy \leq C_1, \qquad (1) $$ and, $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} v_i^{2+\gamma} dy \leq C_2, \qquad (2) $$ In particular, we have, using the Nash-Moser iterate scheme, the following inequality: $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon/2}(0)} |
abla (\eta v_i^{ rac{1+\gamma}{2}})|^2 \leq C_3, \qquad (3) $$ where $ \eta $ is a cutoff function. With the Sobolev embeding, we obtain: $$ || v_i||_{L^q(B_{k+\epsilon/4})} \leq C_q \qquad (4) $$ Also, we choose (because of Brezis-Merle result) $ r_0 $ such that, $ u_i 	o -\infty $ on $ \partial B_{r_0} $ and thus $ v_i 	o 0 $ on $ \partial B_{r_0} $.  igskip We use the Green representation formula to have: $$ v_i(0)=\int_{B_{r_0}(0)} G_0(0,y)(v_i^2-|
abla u_i|^2 v_i) dy + \int_{\partial B_{r_0}(0)} \partial_{
u} G_0(0, s) v_i ds $$ Here, $ G_0 $ is the Green function of the Laplacian with Dirichlet condition on $ B_{r_0} $. We can write, $ G_0(x,y)=-\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |x-y|+H_0(x,y) $. For $ x \in B_{1/2+\epsilon/6} $ and $ y \in B_{r_0} $, $ G_0 \in L^q, \,\, orall q \geq 1 $. We use Holder inequality and $ (1) $, $ (2) $ or $ 4 $ to obtain: $$ v_i(0) \leq ||G_0(0,.)||_{L^q}||v_i||_{L^p}+ C_4||v_i||_{L^{\infty}(\partial B_{r_0})} \leq C_5 $$ which contradict the fact that : $$ v_i(0) =e^{u_i(0)} 	o + \infty $$ Thus, for all $ \gamma >0 $ : $$ \gamma u_i(0) + u_i(\epsilon) 	o +\infty. $$ This means that, for our particular sequence: $$ u_i(0)+u_i(1) 	o +\infty, $$ it is impossible. Thus: $$ \lim_i \left ( \inf_{x, y \in B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} G_i(x,y)ight ) =0. $$
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a positive Green lower bound gives $L^p$ bounds on $e^{u_i}$ via Nash-Moser and Sobolev, so the Green representation bounds $e^{u_i(0)}$, contradicting blow-up.

nodes.name: Contradiction target
nodes.statement: We want to prove by contradiction that: \bigskip For all $ 1 > \epsilon >0 $ and $ \gamma >0 $ , there is a constant $ c= c(b, C, \epsilon, \gamma) $ such that: $$ \gamma u_i(0) + u_i(\epsilon) \to + \infty, $$
nodes.statement_short: State the claim to be argued by contradiction

nodes.name: Introduce v_i = e^{u_i}
nodes.statement: For this, we consider the function: $$ v_i=e^{u_i} $$ $$ -\Delta v_i + |\nabla u_i|^2 v_i= v_i^2. $$
nodes.statement_short: Set $v_i=e^{u_i}$ and write its equation

nodes.name: Rewrite with coercive operator and Green representation
nodes.statement: Also, we can write: $$ -\Delta v_i + (1+ |\nabla u_i|^2) v_i= v_i^2+ v_i, $$ And, $$ \inf_{B_k(0)} v_i \geq \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} G_i(y_i,y)(v_i^2+ v_i ) dy $$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite with $-\Delta+\epsilon_i$ and bound $\inf v_i$ via its Green function

nodes.name: Suppose positive Green lower bound
nodes.statement: Thus, by contradiction, we suppose that: $$ \lim_i \left ( \inf_{x, y \in B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} G_i(x,y)\right ) > c >0, $$ thus, $$ \sup_{B_1(0)} e^{\gamma u_i} \times v_i (k) \geq c \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)}(v_i^{2+\gamma}+ v_i^{1+\gamma} ) dy, $$
nodes.statement_short: Assume a positive Green lower bound and derive an integral inequality

nodes.name: Suppose sup + inf finite
nodes.statement: If we argue by contradiction, and suppose that $ \sup + \inf $ is finite: $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} v_i^{1+\gamma} dy \leq C_1, \qquad (1) $$ and, $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} v_i^{2+\gamma} dy \leq C_2, \qquad (2) $$
nodes.statement_short: Assume sup+inf finite, giving integral bounds (1), (2)

nodes.name: Nash-Moser estimate
nodes.statement: In particular, we have, using the Nash-Moser iterate scheme, the following inequality: $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon/2}(0)} |\nabla (\eta v_i^{\frac{1+\gamma}{2}})|^2 \leq C_3, \qquad (3) $$ where $ \eta $ is a cutoff function.
nodes.statement_short: Nash-Moser iteration gives gradient bound (3)

nodes.name: Sobolev embedding
nodes.statement: With the Sobolev embeding, we obtain: $$ || v_i||_{L^q(B_{k+\epsilon/4})} \leq C_q \qquad (4) $$
nodes.statement_short: Sobolev embedding gives $L^q$ bound (4)

nodes.name: Choose r_0 via Brezis-Merle
nodes.statement: Also, we choose (because of Brezis-Merle result) $ r_0 $ such that, $ u_i \to -\infty $ on $ \partial B_{r_0} $ and thus $ v_i \to 0 $ on $ \partial B_{r_0} $.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $r_0$ with $v_i\to0$ on $\partial B_{r_0}$ by Brezis-Merle

nodes.name: Green representation of v_i(0)
nodes.statement: We use the Green representation formula to have: $$ v_i(0)=\int_{B_{r_0}(0)} G_0(0,y)(v_i^2-|\nabla u_i|^2 v_i) dy + \int_{\partial B_{r_0}(0)} \partial_{\nu} G_0(0, s) v_i ds $$ Here, $ G_0 $ is the Green function of the Laplacian with Dirichlet condition on $ B_{r_0} $. We can write, $ G_0(x,y)=-\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |x-y|+H_0(x,y) $. For $ x \in B_{1/2+\epsilon/6} $ and $ y \in B_{r_0} $, $ G_0 \in L^q, \,\,\forall q \geq 1 $.
nodes.statement_short: Green representation of $v_i(0)$ on $B_{r_0}$

nodes.name: Holder bound and contradiction
nodes.statement: We use Holder inequality and $ (1) $, $ (2) $ or $ 4 $ to obtain: $$ v_i(0) \leq ||G_0(0,.)||_{L^q}||v_i||_{L^p}+ C_4||v_i||_{L^{\infty}(\partial B_{r_0})} \leq C_5 $$ which contradict the fact that : $$ v_i(0) =e^{u_i(0)} \to + \infty $$
nodes.statement_short: Holder bounds $v_i(0)$, contradicting $v_i(0)\to\infty$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus, for all $ \gamma >0 $ : $$ \gamma u_i(0) + u_i(\epsilon) \to +\infty. $$ This means that, for our particular sequence: $$ u_i(0)+u_i(1) \to +\infty, $$ it is impossible. Thus: $$ \lim_i \left ( \inf_{x, y \in B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} G_i(x,y)\right ) =0. $$
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the Green function infimum tends to 0

nodes.name: Equation (1)
nodes.statement: $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} v_i^{1+\gamma} dy \leq C_1, \qquad (1) $$

nodes.name: Equation (2)
nodes.statement: $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon}(0)} v_i^{2+\gamma} dy \leq C_2, \qquad (2) $$

nodes.name: Equation (3)
nodes.statement: $$ \int_{B_{k+\epsilon/2}(0)} |\nabla (\eta v_i^{\frac{1+\gamma}{2}})|^2 \leq C_3, \qquad (3) $$

nodes.name: Equation (4)
nodes.statement: $$ || v_i||_{L^q(B_{k+\epsilon/4})} \leq C_q \qquad (4) $$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: \underbar {Proof of the theorem 1} \bigskip Let's consider the sequence $ (u_i)_i $ on the ball of radius 2. \bigskip Now, suppose that, we are in the case 3) of the Brezis-Merle result. We assume that, $ \Omega= B_2(0) $, and, $ 0 \leq |x_0| \leq |x_1| \leq \ldots \leq |x_m| \leq 1/3 $ We denote by $ G $ the Green function of the lapalcian on the unit ball. We use the Green representation formula for $ u_i $, we obtain: $$ u_i(y_i)=\max_{\Omega} u_i= \int_{B_1(0)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy + \int_{\partial B_1(0)} \partial_{\nu} G(y_i, s) u_i ds $$ We can use the fact that (Brezis-Merle) $ u_i\to -\infty $ on $ \Omega-\cup_{k=1}^m B(x_k, r_k) $, to have: $$ \int_{B_1(0)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy= \sum_{k=1}^m \int_{B(x_k, r_k)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy +\int_{\Omega-\cup_{k=1}^m B(x_k, r_k)} G(x_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy = $$ $$= \sum_{k=1}^m \int_{B(x_k, r_k)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy+ o(1), $$ Without loss of generality, we can assume that $ y_i \to x_0 $. Thus, for $ k\not=0 $, $ G(y_i, y) \to \beta_k >0 $ for $ y \in B(x_k, r_k) $. We are concerned by the case $ y\in B(x_0, r_0) $. In this case, we can write: $$ \int_{B(x_0, r_0)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy \leq \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy =\int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log \dfrac{|1-\bar y_iy|}{|y_i-y|} V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy $$ But, $$ |1-\bar y_iy| \to \beta_0 >0, y \in B(x_0, r_0), $$ Thus, $$ \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy \leq C(\beta, b, C)+ \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |y_i-y| V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy $$ We do a blow-up around $ y_i $, we write $$ y= y_i+xe^{-u_i(y_i)/2}, $$ $$ \tilde u_i(x)= u_i( y_i+xe^{-u_i(y_i)/2})-u_i(y_i), $$ and, $$ \tilde V_i(x)= V_i( y_i+xe^{-u_i(y_i)/2}). $$ We have, $$ \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |y_i-y| V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy = \dfrac{u_i(y_i)}{4\pi} \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} \tilde V_ie^{\tilde u_i} dx + $$ $$ + \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |x| \tilde V_i e^{\tilde u_i} dx , $$ The fact that $ e^{\tilde u_i} \leq 1 $ and $ -\log |x| \leq 0 $ for $ |x| \geq 1 $, we can write: $$ \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |x| \tilde V_i e^{\tilde u_i} dx \leq C, $$ Also, we can see that, in the case $ V_i \to V $ in $ C^0(\Omega) $, by the result of YY.Li and I. Shafrir, we have: $$ \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} \tilde V_ie^{\tilde u_i} dx =\int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} V_ie^{u_i} dy \to 8\pi m \leq bC, \,\,m \in {\mathbb N}^* $$ Finaly, we can write: $$ u_i(y_i) \leq (2m+\epsilon) u_i(y_i) + \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i + C_1, $$ Thus, $$ C_2(bC) \sup_{\Omega} u_i +\sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i\geq -C_3, $$ But, $$ \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \to -\infty, $$ Thus, by the classical Harnack inequality, we can have: $$ \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \leq C_4 \inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i + C_5, $$ Finaly, for all compact set $ K $, there are two positive constants $ C_1'= C_1'(dist(K, \partial \Omega), b, C) $ and $ C_2'=C_2'(K, \Omega, b, C) $ such that: $$ \sup_{\Omega} u_i + C_1'\inf_K u_i\geq -C_2', $$ In general, the condition $ V_i \to V $ in $ C^0(\Omega) $ can be removed and replaced by the Brezis-Merle consequence of blow-up phenomenon. $$ \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} \tilde V_ie^{\tilde u_i} dx =\int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} V_ie^{u_i} dy \to 4\pi \tilde \alpha_0 \leq bC, \,\, \tilde \alpha_0 \geq 1. $$
nodes.statement_short: Green representation at the maximum point, splitting the mass near blow-up points; a blow-up rescaling bounds $u_i(y_i)$ by a multiple of itself plus boundary values, then Harnack on the boundary.

nodes.name: Reduce to case 3 on B_2
nodes.statement: Let's consider the sequence $ (u_i)_i $ on the ball of radius 2. \bigskip Now, suppose that, we are in the case 3) of the Brezis-Merle result. We assume that, $ \Omega= B_2(0) $, and, $ 0 \leq |x_0| \leq |x_1| \leq \ldots \leq |x_m| \leq 1/3 $
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the blow-up case 3) on $B_2(0)$ with blow-up points in $B_{1/3}$

nodes.name: Green representation at the maximum
nodes.statement: We denote by $ G $ the Green function of the lapalcian on the unit ball. We use the Green representation formula for $ u_i $, we obtain: $$ u_i(y_i)=\max_{\Omega} u_i= \int_{B_1(0)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy + \int_{\partial B_1(0)} \partial_{\nu} G(y_i, s) u_i ds $$
nodes.statement_short: Green representation of $u_i$ at its maximum point $y_i$

nodes.name: Localize mass at blow-up points
nodes.statement: We can use the fact that (Brezis-Merle) $ u_i\to -\infty $ on $ \Omega-\cup_{k=1}^m B(x_k, r_k) $, to have: $$ \int_{B_1(0)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy= \sum_{k=1}^m \int_{B(x_k, r_k)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy +\int_{\Omega-\cup_{k=1}^m B(x_k, r_k)} G(x_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy = $$ $$= \sum_{k=1}^m \int_{B(x_k, r_k)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy+ o(1), $$
nodes.statement_short: Brezis-Merle: the integral concentrates on balls around blow-up points

nodes.name: WLOG y_i -> x_0
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we can assume that $ y_i \to x_0 $. Thus, for $ k\not=0 $, $ G(y_i, y) \to \beta_k >0 $ for $ y \in B(x_k, r_k) $.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $y_i\to x_0$; other blow-up balls give bounded Green values

nodes.name: Bound the integral near x_0
nodes.statement: We are concerned by the case $ y\in B(x_0, r_0) $. In this case, we can write: $$ \int_{B(x_0, r_0)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy \leq \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy =\int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log \dfrac{|1-\bar y_iy|}{|y_i-y|} V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy $$ But, $$ |1-\bar y_iy| \to \beta_0 >0, y \in B(x_0, r_0), $$ Thus, $$ \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} G(y_i,y) V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy \leq C(\beta, b, C)+ \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |y_i-y| V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the Green integral near $x_0$ by the log singularity

nodes.name: Blow-up rescaling
nodes.statement: We do a blow-up around $ y_i $, we write $$ y= y_i+xe^{-u_i(y_i)/2}, $$ $$ \tilde u_i(x)= u_i( y_i+xe^{-u_i(y_i)/2})-u_i(y_i), $$ and, $$ \tilde V_i(x)= V_i( y_i+xe^{-u_i(y_i)/2}). $$
nodes.statement_short: Rescale around $y_i$

nodes.name: Split the rescaled integral
nodes.statement: We have, $$ \int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |y_i-y| V_ie^{u_i(y)}dy = \dfrac{u_i(y_i)}{4\pi} \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} \tilde V_ie^{\tilde u_i} dx + $$ $$ + \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |x| \tilde V_i e^{\tilde u_i} dx , $$ The fact that $ e^{\tilde u_i} \leq 1 $ and $ -\log |x| \leq 0 $ for $ |x| \geq 1 $, we can write: $$ \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} -\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \log |x| \tilde V_i e^{\tilde u_i} dx \leq C, $$
nodes.statement_short: Split the rescaled integral; the $\log|x|$ part is bounded

nodes.name: Mass quantization (Li-Shafrir)
nodes.statement: Also, we can see that, in the case $ V_i \to V $ in $ C^0(\Omega) $, by the result of YY.Li and I. Shafrir, we have: $$ \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} \tilde V_ie^{\tilde u_i} dx =\int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} V_ie^{u_i} dy \to 8\pi m \leq bC, \,\,m \in {\mathbb N}^* $$
nodes.statement_short: Li-Shafrir: the mass tends to $8\pi m\le bC$

nodes.name: Bound u_i(y_i) and boundary values
nodes.statement: Finaly, we can write: $$ u_i(y_i) \leq (2m+\epsilon) u_i(y_i) + \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i + C_1, $$ Thus, $$ C_2(bC) \sup_{\Omega} u_i +\sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i\geq -C_3, $$ But, $$ \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \to -\infty, $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $u_i(y_i)$ by a multiple of itself plus the boundary sup

nodes.name: Harnack on the boundary
nodes.statement: Thus, by the classical Harnack inequality, we can have: $$ \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \leq C_4 \inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i + C_5, $$
nodes.statement_short: Classical Harnack inequality on $\partial B_1$

nodes.name: Conclude sup + C inf
nodes.statement: Finaly, for all compact set $ K $, there are two positive constants $ C_1'= C_1'(dist(K, \partial \Omega), b, C) $ and $ C_2'=C_2'(K, \Omega, b, C) $ such that: $$ \sup_{\Omega} u_i + C_1'\inf_K u_i\geq -C_2', $$
nodes.statement_short: Obtain $\sup_\Omega u_i + C_1'\inf_K u_i\ge -C_2'$

nodes.name: Remove continuity of V_i
nodes.statement: In general, the condition $ V_i \to V $ in $ C^0(\Omega) $ can be removed and replaced by the Brezis-Merle consequence of blow-up phenomenon. $$ \int_{B(0, (r_0+ \epsilon) e^{u_i(y_i)/2})} \tilde V_ie^{\tilde u_i} dx =\int_{B(y_i, r_0+ \epsilon)} V_ie^{u_i} dy \to 4\pi \tilde \alpha_0 \leq bC, \,\, \tilde \alpha_0 \geq 1. $$
nodes.statement_short: Replace $V_i\to V$ by the Brezis-Merle mass bound $4\pi\tilde\alpha_0$

nodes.name: Example of situation 1 of the theorem
nodes.statement: { \bf Remark}: {\it an example of the situation 1 of the theorem 2:} \bigskip Let's consider the following sequence of functions, on $ \Omega = B_1(0) $; $$ u_{\epsilon}(r)= \log \dfrac{1}{(\mu_{\epsilon}^2+ r^2)^2} \,\,\, { \rm with} \,\,\mu_{\epsilon} \to +\infty $$ Then, for $ K = B_k(0) $ with $ 0 < k <1 $, we have: $$ -\Delta u_{\epsilon} = e^{u_{\epsilon}} \,\,\, { \rm and}, $$ $$ \sup_{K} u_{\epsilon} \to - \infty, $$ $$ \sup_{\Omega} u_{\epsilon} + \inf_K u_{\epsilon} \to - \infty $$
nodes.statement_short: Radial solutions $u_\epsilon=\log(1/(\mu_\epsilon^2+r^2)^2)$, $\mu_\epsilon\to\infty$, with $\sup_K u_\epsilon\to-\infty$ (case 1 of the theorem).

nodes.name: Sharp sup + inf inequality (Question 1a)
nodes.statement: 1) a) Can we have the following sharp inequality: $$ \sup_{\Omega} u_i + \inf_K u_i \geq C_1=C_1(b, C, K, \Omega) \,\, ? $$
nodes.statement_short: Does $\sup_\Omega u_i+\inf_K u_i\ge C_1(b,C,K,\Omega)$ hold (coefficient 1)?

nodes.name: Shafrir's example
nodes.statement: We look to the following example of I. Shafrir, see [7]: $$ u(r)= \begin{cases} 2\log \left ( \dfrac{2\beta r^{\beta -1}}{1+r^{2\beta}}\right )\,\, \text{if } \,\, r >1 \,\, \\ 2\log \beta + 2\log \left ( \dfrac{2}{1+r^2}\right )\,\, \text{if } \,\, r \leq 1 . \end{cases} $$ We take $ u_i(r)=u(ir)+2\log i $. Then, if we take $ \beta >1 $, we have: $$ -\Delta u_i = \begin{cases} 2 e^{u_i} \,\, \text{if }\,\, r >1/i \,\, \\ \dfrac{2}{{\beta}^2}e^{u_i}\,\, \text{if } \,\, r \leq 1/i. \end{cases} $$ $$ u_i(0) \to + \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, u_i(k) \to - \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, u_i(0) + u_i(k) \to - \infty. $$
nodes.statement_short: Shafrir's piecewise radial example with $\beta>1$ has $u_i(0)+u_i(k)\to-\infty$, so the sharp inequality fails.

nodes.name: Sharp inequality with more regular V_i (Question 1b)
nodes.statement: b) Perhaps with more regularity on $ V_i $ ?

nodes.name: Brezis-Li-Shafrir example
nodes.statement: With the previous example, we can use the example of Brezis-Li-Sahfrir, see [2], to construct two sequences of functions $ (u_i)_i $ and $ (V_i)_i $ ( $ 1< \beta=\beta_i \searrow 1 $), such that: $$ -\Delta u_i = V_i e^{u_i} \,\, { \rm in} \,\, B_1(0), $$ $$ C^1(B_1(0)) \ni V_i \to V\equiv 2 \,\, { \rm in} \,\, C^0(B_1(0)), $$ $$ u_i(0) \to + \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, u_i(k) \to - \infty, $$ and we have: $$ \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, u_i(0) + u_i(k) \to - \infty. $$
nodes.statement_short: With $\beta_i\searrow1$, $V_i\to2$ in $C^0$ yet $u_i(0)+u_i(k)\to-\infty$.

nodes.name: Sharp inequality for -Delta u = e^u (Question 1c)
nodes.statement: c) Perhaps, if we consider the solutions to the following equation: $$ -\Delta u_i = e^{u_i} \,\, { \rm in} \,\, \Omega $$

nodes.name: Chen's two-bubble example: sup + inf unbounded below
nodes.statement: Consider the situation of X.Chen, see [5]. First we can have a blowing-up sequence $ \tilde u_i $, with two blow-up points, for example $ z_0=0 $ and $ z_1=1 $ and associeted radii $ r_i \to + \infty $, such that: $$ e^{ \tilde u_i} \to \sum_{k=0}^1 8\pi \delta_{z_k}, , $$ and, $$ \tilde u_i \to - \infty , \,\, { \rm on \, each \, compact \, set \, of }\,\, B_{r_i}-\{0, 1\}. $$ $$ \int_{B_{r_i}} e^{ \tilde u_i} dx \to 16\pi. $$ It is clear that we can choose the radius $ r_i $ such that : $$ r_i << \tilde u_i(0). $$ Now, in the situation of the paper of X.Chen, we take the following sequence: $$ u_i(y)= \tilde u_i(r_iy)+ 2 \log r_i. $$ In this case, we have one exterior blow-up point $ 0 $ and two interior blow-up points $ 0 $ and $ z_i=1/(r_i) $, in the unit ball, and, $$ e^{u_i} \to 16\pi \delta_{0}, $$ Let's consider the Green function of the unit ball, $ G $: $$ G(x, y)=\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log \dfrac{|1-\bar xy|}{|x-y|}, $$ We write: $$ u_i(0)= \int_{B_1(0)} G(0,y) e^{u_i} dy + \int_{\partial B_1(0)} \partial_{\nu} G(0, \sigma) u_i(\sigma) d\sigma, $$ hence, $$ u_i(0)\geq \int_{B_{l_i^0 r_i^0}(0)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |y| e^{u_i} dy+ \int_{B_{l_i^1 r_i^1}(z_i)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |y| e^{u_i} dy + \inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i, $$ where, $$ r_i^0 = e^{-u_i(0)/2}, $$ $$ r_i^1 = e^{-u_i(z_i)/2}, $$ and, $$ l_i^0 r_i^0 \leq \dfrac{1}{2} |z_i|, $$ $$ l_i^1 r_i^1 \leq \dfrac{1}{2} |z_i|, $$ we can choose $ l_i^0 $ as in the paper of CC.Chen and C.S Lin, see [4] (see also the formulation of Li-Shafrir, [6]), to obtain the following estimates: $$ \int_{B_{l_i^0 r_i^0}(0)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |y| e^{u_i} dy = \dfrac{u_i(0)}{4 \pi} \int_{B_{l_i^0}} e^{v_i} dt + \int_{B_{l_i^0}} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |t| e^{v_i} dt, $$ with, $$ \int_{B_{l_i^0}} e^{v_i} dt \geq 8\pi-\dfrac{C}{L_i^s}-\dfrac{C}{u_i(0)}, $$ and, $$ \int_{B_{l_i^0}} \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |t| e^{v_i} dt \leq C,$$ where, $ v_i $ is the blow-up function around $ 0 $: $$ v_i(t)=u_i(e^{-u_i(0)/2} t)-u_i(0). $$ With, $$ (L_i)^s= ((1/2) |z_i| e^{u_i(0)/2})^s =((1/2 r_i) r_i e^{\tilde u_i(0)/2})^s=(1/2)^se^{s\tilde u_i(0)/2} >> \tilde u_i(0)+ 2 \log r_i = u_i(0) . $$ For the term: $$ \int_{B_{l_i^1 r_i^1}(z_i)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |y| e^{u_i} dy, $$ We take, $$ w_i(t)=u_i(e^{-u_i(z_i)/2} t+z_i)-u_i(z_i), $$ we have: $$ \int_{B_{l_i^1 r_i^1}(z_i)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |y| e^{u_i} dy = \int_{B_{l_i^1}(0)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |t r_i^1+z_i| e^{w_i} dt, $$ which we can write as: $$ \int_{B_{l_i^1}(0)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |t r_i^1+z_i| e^{w_i} dt =-\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |z_i | \int_{B_{l_i^1}(0)} e^{w_i} dt+\int_{B_{l_i^1}(0)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |\dfrac{t r_i^1}{z_i}+1| e^{w_i} dt, $$ but, $$ l_i^1 r_i^1 \leq \dfrac{1}{2} |z_i|, $$ Thus the term $ \log |\dfrac{t r_i^1}{z_i}+1| $ is bounded. And we have: $$ \int_{B_{l_i^1 r_i^1}(z_i)} -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |y| e^{u_i} dy \geq -\dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \log |z_i | \int_{B_{l_i^1}(0)} e^{w_i} dt- C, $$ because: $$ \int_{B_{l_i^1}(0)} e^{w_i} dt \to 8 \pi. $$ Finally, we obtain the following inequality: $$ u_i(0) \geq 2 u_i(0)+ \inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i - ( 4-\epsilon) \log |z_i | - C, $$ which we can write as: $$ u_i(0) + \inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \leq ( 4-\epsilon) \log |z_i | + C \to -\infty , $$ Thus, $$ \sup_{\Omega } u_i + \inf_{ B_1(0)} u_i = u_i(0)+ \inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \to -\infty. $$ Here, we have choosen the Green function of the unit ball. The same argument may be applied to a ball of radius $ 1 \geq r > 0 $, to have: $$ \sup_{\Omega } u_i + \inf_{ B_r(0)} u_i = u_i(0)+ \inf_{\partial B_r(0)} u_i \to -\infty. $$ Thus, we have an example of blowing-up sequence with finite volume (conformal volume) and the $ \sup + \inf $ is not bounded below by a constant.
nodes.statement_short: Rescaling Chen's two-bubble solutions of $-\Delta u=e^u$ gives a finite-volume blowing-up sequence with $\sup+\inf\to-\infty$.

nodes.name: Removing condition (**) (Question 2)
nodes.statement: 2) What's happen if we remove the condition $ (**) $ of the problem: $$ \int_{\Omega} e^{u_i} dx \leq C \,\,\, ?$$

nodes.name: Example without volume bound
nodes.statement: Here, we can use the example: $$ u(r)= \begin{cases} 2\log \left ( \dfrac{2\beta r^{\beta -1}}{1+r^{2\beta}}\right )\,\, \text{if } \,\, r >1 \,\, \\ 2\log \beta + 2\log \left ( \dfrac{2}{1+r^2}\right )\,\, \text{if } \,\, r \leq 1 . \end{cases} $$ We take $ u_i(r)=u(ir)+2\log i $. Then, if we replace $ \beta $ by $ i $, we have: $$ -\Delta u_i = \begin{cases} 2 e^{u_i} \,\, \text{if }\,\, r >1/i \,\, \\ \dfrac{2}{i^2}e^{u_i}\,\, \text{if } \,\, r \leq 1/i. \end{cases} $$ $$ u_i(0) \to + \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, u_i(k) \to - \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, C >0, \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, u_i(0) + C u_i(k) \to - \infty $$ and, $$ \int_{B_1(0)} e^{u_i} dx \geq C' i \to + \infty, $$
nodes.statement_short: Shafrir's example with $\beta=i$: $u_i(0)+Cu_i(k)\to-\infty$ for all $C$, with unbounded volume.

nodes.name: Replacing (*) by 0 < a <= V_i <= b (Question 3)
nodes.statement: 3) Can we replace it, as in the paper of Brezis-Merle, by the following condition: $$ 0 < a \leq V_i(x) \leq b \,\,? \qquad (***) $$

nodes.name: Annulus example with 0 < a <= V_i <= b
nodes.statement: Here, we can use the example: $$ u_i(r)=2\log \left ( \dfrac{2i r^{i -1}}{1+r^{2i}}\right )\,\, \text{if } \,\, 1\leq r \leq 2. $$ We have: $$ -\Delta u_i = 2 e^{u_i} \,\, \text{if }\,\, 1\leq r \leq 2. $$ $$ u_i(1) \to + \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, 1 <k \leq 2 \,\, u_i(k) \to - \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, C >0, \forall \,\, 1 <k \leq 2,\,\, u_i(1) + C u_i(k) \to - \infty $$ and, $$ \int_{ \{ x, 1\leq |x| \leq 2\} } e^{u_i} dx \geq C' i \to + \infty, $$
nodes.statement_short: On the annulus $1\le r\le2$, $u_i=2\log(2ir^{i-1}/(1+r^{2i}))$ gives $u_i(1)+Cu_i(k)\to-\infty$ with unbounded volume.

nodes.name: Radial case: sup + inf inequality holds
nodes.statement: Consider on the unit ball, the radial solutions to the previous equation with the following condition: $$ u_i(0) \to + \infty, $$ $$ \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, u_i(k) \to - \infty, $$ $$ \int_{B_1(0)} e^{u_i} dx \leq C. $$ Then we have: $$ \inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i =\sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i = u_i(1), $$ This means: $$ \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i-\inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i = 0, $$ All the conditions of the paper of YY.Li, see [7], (on riemannian surfaces) are satisfied and thus, we have: $$ \forall \,\, 0 <k \leq 1,\,\, |u_i(0)+ u_i(k)| \leq c=c(C, k), $$
nodes.statement_short: Radial blowing-up solutions with bounded volume have constant boundary values, so YY. Li's Harnack result gives $|u_i(0)+u_i(k)|\le c$.

nodes.name: YY.Li condition
nodes.statement: For the general case when we assume that the prescribed scalar curvature $ V_i $ uniformly lipschitzian, it is sufficient to prove the YY.Li condition: $$ \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i-\inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \leq B. $$
nodes.statement_short: YY. Li condition: bounded oscillation $\sup_{\partial B_1}u_i-\inf_{\partial B_1}u_i\le B$, sufficient for Lipschitz $V_i$.

nodes.name: YY.Li condition holds on closed surfaces
nodes.statement: Note that, in the case of compact riemannian surfaces without boundary, the last condition hold and then, the $ \sup + \inf $ inequality hold.
assumptions: in the case of compact riemannian surfaces without boundary
conclusions: the last condition hold and then, the $ \sup + \inf $ inequality hold.

nodes.name: sup + inf for blow-up with volume at most 8 pi
nodes.statement: Now, assume we are on a compact riemannian surface without boundary. Assmue that the sequence blow-up and we have the following inequality: $$ \int_{M} V_i e^{u_i} dx \leq 8\pi. $$ Then, we have a $ \sup + \inf $ inequality.
assumptions: assume we are on a compact riemannian surface without boundary
the sequence blow-up and we have the following inequality: $$ \int_{M} V_i e^{u_i} dx \leq 8\pi. $$

nodes.name: C sup + inf inequality on closed surfaces
nodes.statement: Now, assume that, on a compact surface without boundary, we have: $$ \int_{M} V_i e^{u_i} dx \leq C, $$ then, $$ C \sup_M u_i + \inf_M u_i \geq -C_2=-C_2(b, C, M). $$
assumptions: on a compact surface without boundary

nodes.name: sup + inf on the unit ball under the YY.Li condition
nodes.statement: If we use YY.Li condition, we can extend this result to the unit ball $ B_1(0) \subset {\mathbb R}^2 $. According to the proof of theorem 2, if we assume for a blowing-up sequence, that: $$ 0 < a \leq V_i(x) \leq b, $$ $$ \int_{B_1(0)} V_i e^{u_i} dx \leq 8\pi, $$ and, $$ \sup_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i-\inf_{\partial B_1(0)} u_i \leq B. $$ Then, the $ \sup + \inf $ inequality hold. We have exactly: $$ \sup_{B_1(0)} u_i+\inf_{B_1(0)} u_i \geq -C=-C(a, b, B). $$
nodes.statement_short: For blowing-up $u_i$ on $B_1$ with $0<a\le V_i\le b$, mass $\le8\pi$ and the YY. Li condition, $\sup+\inf\ge -C(a,b,B)$.

nodes.name: C_1 independent of K (Question 4)
nodes.statement: 4) Is it possible to have $ C_1 $ independant of the compact $ K $ ?

nodes.name: C_1 independent of K under the YY.Li condition
nodes.statement: This is the case if we suppose the YY.Li condition satisfied.
assumptions: we suppose the YY.Li condition satisfied

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.1
nodes.statement: For example, on a compact riemannian surface $ M $ without boundary, if we consider the following equation: $$ -\Delta u_i + R = V_ie^{u_i}, $$ with, $ V_i $ such that: $$ 0 < a \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \,\, { \rm on} \,\, M, $$ we have after integration of the equation that: $$ \forall \,\, \Omega \subset M, \,\, 0 < a \int_{\Omega} e^{u_i} dx \leq a \int_{M} e^{u_i} dx \,\, \leq \int_{M} R(x) dx \leq |M| \sup_{M} R, $$ Also, we have: $$ 0 < \int_{M} R(x) dx = \int_{M} V_i e^{u_i} dx \leq b e^{\sup_{M} u_i}, $$ thus, $$ \sup_{M} u_i \geq \log \left ( \dfrac{\int_{M} R(x) dx}{b} \right ) . $$ Thus, we are in the case of theorem 2 and the point 1) of this theorem is not possible. We have the following:
nodes.statement_short: Integrating $-\Delta u_i+R=V_ie^{u_i}$ gives a lower bound on $\sup_M u_i$, excluding case 1) of the theorem.

nodes.name: Integrate the equation
nodes.statement: For example, on a compact riemannian surface $ M $ without boundary, if we consider the following equation: $$ -\Delta u_i + R = V_ie^{u_i}, $$ with, $ V_i $ such that: $$ 0 < a \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \,\, { \rm on} \,\, M, $$ we have after integration of the equation that: $$ \forall \,\, \Omega \subset M, \,\, 0 < a \int_{\Omega} e^{u_i} dx \leq a \int_{M} e^{u_i} dx \,\, \leq \int_{M} R(x) dx \leq |M| \sup_{M} R, $$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the equation to bound the volume

nodes.name: Lower bound on sup u_i
nodes.statement: Also, we have: $$ 0 < \int_{M} R(x) dx = \int_{M} V_i e^{u_i} dx \leq b e^{\sup_{M} u_i}, $$ thus, $$ \sup_{M} u_i \geq \log \left ( \dfrac{\int_{M} R(x) dx}{b} \right ) . $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\sup_M u_i$ from below

nodes.name: Conclude via the theorem
nodes.statement: Thus, we are in the case of theorem 2 and the point 1) of this theorem is not possible. We have the following:
nodes.statement_short: Case 1) of the theorem is excluded, so case 2) holds

nodes.name: sup + C inf on a surface with 0 < a <= V_i <= b
nodes.statement: Let $ (u_i) $ and $ (V_i) $ two sequences of functions solutions to the previous problem on a riemannian surface $ M $ , such that, we have only the following condition: $$ 0 < a \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \qquad (***) $$ then, there are two positive constants $ C_1=C_1(a, b, M) $ and $ C_2=C_2(a, b, M) $ such that: $$ \sup_{M} u_i + C_1\inf_M u_i \geq -C_2, $$
assumptions: $ (u_i) $ and $ (V_i) $ two sequences of functions solutions to the previous problem on a riemannian surface $ M $
conclusions: there are two positive constants $ C_1=C_1(a, b, M) $ and $ C_2=C_2(a, b, M) $ such that: $$ \sup_{M} u_i + C_1\inf_M u_i \geq -C_2, $$
nodes.statement_short: On a surface with $0<a\le V_i\le b$, $\sup_M u_i + C_1\inf_M u_i\ge -C_2$.

nodes.name: Condition (***)
nodes.statement: $$ 0 < a \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \qquad (***) $$

nodes.name: sup + C inf inequality via maximum principle (previous paper)
nodes.statement: Note that in the previous paper, by using the maximum principle, we have proved that if we consider on compact riemannian surface without boundary the following equation: $$ -\Delta u_i + R = V_ie^{u_i}, $$ with, $ V_i $ such that: $$ a=0 \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \,\, { \rm on} \,\, M, $$ Then we have an inequality of type: $$ \sup_{M} u_i + C_1\inf_M u_i \geq -C_2, $$ with $ C_1=C_1(b, M) $ and $ C_2=C_2(b, M) $.
conclusions: with $ C_1=C_1(b, M) $ and $ C_2=C_2(b, M) $
nodes.statement_short: On a closed surface with $0\le V_i\le b$, $\sup_M u_i + C_1\inf_M u_i\ge -C_2$ with constants depending on $b,M$.

nodes.name: Recover the previous result by the argument of the theorem
nodes.statement: Can we try to find this result with the previous argument of the theorem 2 ?

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.2
nodes.statement: We have, $$ \int_{M} V_i e^{u_i} dx = \int_{M} R(x) dx \leq |M| \sup_{M} R = C, $$ We can say that, after using the proof of theorem 2 and the YY.Li inequality around the maximum of $ u_i $: $$ \forall \,\Omega, \,\, \sup_{\partial \Omega} u_i-\inf_{\partial \Omega} u_i \leq C', $$ that,
nodes.statement_short: Total mass equals $\int_M R$; the proof of the theorem plus YY. Li's bounded boundary oscillation give the inequality.

nodes.name: (int R / 4 pi - 1) sup + inf inequality
nodes.statement: Let $ (u_i) $ and $ (V_i) $ two sequences of functions solutions to the previous problem on a riemannian surface $ M $ without boundary, such that, we have only the following condition: $$ 0 \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \qquad (****) $$ then, there is a positive constant $ C_1=C_1(b, M) $ such that: $$ \left (\dfrac{\int_M R}{4\pi}-1 \right ) \sup_{M} u_i + \inf_M u_i \geq -C_1, $$
assumptions: $ (u_i) $ and $ (V_i) $ two sequences of functions solutions to the previous problem on a riemannian surface $ M $ without boundary
conclusions: there is a positive constant $ C_1=C_1(b, M) $ such that: $$ \left (\dfrac{\int_M R}{4\pi}-1 \right ) \sup_{M} u_i + \inf_M u_i \geq -C_1, $$
nodes.statement_short: On a closed surface with $0\le V_i\le b$, $(\int_M R/4\pi-1)\sup_M u_i+\inf_M u_i\ge -C_1$.

nodes.name: Condition (****)
nodes.statement: $$ 0 \leq V_i(x) \leq b, \qquad (****) $$

nodes.name: Constant curvature, unit volume case
nodes.statement: This is the wellknown inequality in a previous paper. To see this, we have assumed in a previous paper that: $$ R \equiv k \in {\mathbb R}_+^*, \,\, {\rm and } \,\, Volume (M)=1, $$ thus, the inequality is : $$ \left (\dfrac{k-4\pi}{4\pi} \right ) \sup_{M} u_i + \inf_M u_i \geq -C_1. $$
nodes.statement_short: With $R\equiv k$ and unit volume, Corollary 2.2 reads $((k-4\pi)/4\pi)\sup_M u_i+\inf_M u_i\ge -C_1$.
